messages:
Mara L.: Proposal: I think we need a harmonized benchmark protocol for head-to-head model compares. Problem right now is too many hidden knobs (tokenizer differences, decode params, KV warm state, kernel choice, batching heuristics). Draft below — seeking quick feedback.

Joel P.: Agree. Can you call out the replay vs synthetic parts? also how we ensure KV cache parity across runs?

Mara L.: Short draft steps: 1) canonical prompt set (fixed seed, fixed stop sequences), 2) tokenizer normalization (force utf-8, merge rules), 3) decode params locked (temp/top_p/penalties), 4) two-phase warm: prefix-warm + KV-warm replay, 5) kernel pinning where possible, 6) identical batching policy or fixed microbatch.

Ravi S.: Quick config I used (for synth + replay):
```
model: "redwood-14b"
decode: {temperature: 0.0, top_p: 0.95, max_new_tokens: 128, stop: ["\n\n"]}
batch: {microbatch: 8, max_batch: 64, timeout_ms: 5}
warm: {prefix_tokens: 32, replay_kv_steps: true}
pin_kernels: ["matmul_v2", "fused_attention"]
```
This gave repeatable p50/p95 numbers.

Alex C.: On kernel pinning: runtime supports --kernel-hint but it still chooses fallback for some seq lengths. For strict parity we can set KERNEL_FORCE env in the harness container; caveat: might break perf if kernel mismatches shape. We should log kernel decision per request.

Tess R.: For batching heuristics, we need two orthogonal modes in the protocol: fixed microbatch (deterministic) and dynamic batching (realistic). Measure both. Metrics: tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, tail-ms, cost-per-1k-tokens. Also collect kernel selection histogram and KV cache hit rate.

Joel P.: How do we make tokenizer alignment deterministic? Minor differences in byte-pair merges change token counts and decode stops. Suggest running a small verification pass: tokenize(prompts) outputs sha256 and token counts for each model before running. If mismatch -> normalize by re-encoding via reference tokenizer.

Mara L.: Good call. Add to protocol: preflight tokenization table + auto-normalize step. Also capture stop-seq behavior by running a deterministic echo test: prompt + stop => ensure stop token encountered at same index.

Ravi S.: Ran a quick AB with replay harness vs synth for the same prompt set yesterday. Results: replay p95 was ~3% higher latency but tokens/sec identical within noise. Kernel histogram showed heavier use of fused attention on replay due to longer prefix lengths. I can share raw traces.

CI Bot: load-harness/2423456789-1: completed. artifacts: https://ci.internal/runs/2423456789-1 :white_check_mark: parity-check: p95 diff 0.8%, token-count diff 0.0%

Alex C.: Please include a small log line format in the protocol for debug: "kernel=<name> seq=<seq_len> microbatch=<n> kv_warm=<true|false>". Makes parsing easier.

Tess R.: Also record cold vs warm run pairs (same workload) to isolate KV warm impact. Recommend 5 cold runs then 20 warm runs.

Mara L.: Next steps: I'll turn this into a short doc (protocol + checklist + minimal harness snippets) and tag @ravi for traces. Can we aim to land a canonical run next Wed?

Joel P.: SGTM. If someone can own kernel-forcing experiments, I'll handle the tokenizer preflight code.

Ravi S.: I can own kernel-forcing experiments. Will drop traces and a small parsing script.

Mara L.: Excellent — thanks everyone. I'll post the draft doc in #eng-runtime and link the run artifacts.

Tess R.: :thumbsup:
